etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French démocrate, from démocratie (modelled on aristocrate (“aristocrat”)), equivalent to demo- +‎ -crat.

definitions.definition: A supporter of democracy; an advocate of democratic politics (originally (historical) as opposed to the aristocrats in Revolutionary France).

quote.citation: 2019 November 25, Kris Cheng, “Hong Kong District Council election: Democrats take control of 17 out of 18 councils in landslide victory”, in Hong Kong Free Press‎[1], archived from the original on 31 July 2020:
quote.text: The democrats now have majority control in almost all areas except the Islands District Council, where they won seven seats, and the pro-Beijing camp obtained 11 seats.

definitions.definition: Someone who rules a representative democracy.

quote.citation: 2011, Wesley Yang, "Death, Dictators, and Democracy", NYU Alumni Magazine, ISSN 1938-4823, issue 16, Spring 2011, page 10:
quote.text: Democrats have to please a large segment of the voting public and will be punished if they fail to provide public goods […] . In the case of autocrats, however, they have to please a small minority of the governing power elite […]  who will punish them if they fail to dedicate the public purse to their private enrichment.

definitions.definition: (US, historical) A large light uncovered wagon with two or more seats.
